introduction.text: The Base del Colosso di Nerone is the remaining foundation of the ancient bronze statue of Nero, a monumental work that once stood near the entrance of Rome’s Domus Aurea and later influenced the naming of the Colosseum. Its ruins illustrate the scale of Roman imperial art and the city’s architectural evolution.

history.description: Construction of the Colossus of Nero by architect Zenodorus between AD 64 and 68.
Vespasian added a radiate crown and renamed the statue Colossus Solis after Nero’s death in AD 68.
Hadrian ordered the statue moved from the Domus Aurea to near the Colosseum around AD 128.
Commodus converted the statue into a depiction of himself as Hercules by replacing the head.
The last certain mention of the statue appears in the Chronography of 354.
The statue was likely destroyed during the Sack of Rome in 410 or toppled by a 5th‑century earthquake.

design.description: The pedestal of the Colossus was a concrete block foundation once covered with marble, later excavated in 1986 and now visible to visitors.

art.description: The Colossus of Nero was a 30‑meter bronze statue, one of the tallest statues of antiquity, depicting the emperor in monumental scale.
